title: The walking isomorphism classifies equivalence arrows of a Segal space
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the Reedy model structure of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A simplicial space is a functor $V:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$. It is a Segal space if it is Reedy fibrant and its consecutive-edge maps $V_n\to V_1\times_{V_0}\cdots\times_{V_0}V_1$ are weak homotopy equivalences for every $n\geq2$. For vertices $x,y$ of $V_0$, let $M_V(x,y)$ be the strict fiber of $(d_1,d_0):V_1\to V_0^2$. The homotopy category $hV$ has those vertices as objects, morphisms $\pi_0M_V(x,y)$, identity from $s_0$, and composition from the degree-two Segal map and $d_1$. Let $V_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq V_1$ be the union of components representing isomorphisms in $hV$.

For $n\geq0$ let $F(n)_k=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([k],[n])$, discrete in the inner direction, and let $cK$ denote the constant simplicial space on a simplicial set $K$. For simplicial spaces $A,V$, use the cartesian internal hom
$$(V^A)_{n,q}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sS}}(A\times F(n)\times c\Delta^q,V),$$
with operators given by precomposition.

Let $I[1]$ be the groupoid on objects $0,1$ with exactly one morphism between each ordered pair, and let $E$ be its ordinary nerve, regarded as a simplicial space discrete in the inner direction. Let $e_0,e_1:F(0)\to E$ select the two objects, and let $a:F(1)\to E$ select the arrow $0\to1$. For every Segal space $V$, restriction along $a$ factors as a natural weak homotopy equivalence
$$\epsilon_V:(V^E)_0\longrightarrow V_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq V_1.$$
It is a map over $V_0^2$: its two endpoint maps are restriction along $e_0,e_1$. The composite $V_0\to(V^E)_0\to V_{\mathrm{eq}}$ induced by the collapse $E\to F(0)$ is $s_0$.

source.place: Theorem 6.2 and its proof in Section 11, with the maps in Section 6; printed pp. 14-15, 24-27. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Write $\operatorname{Map}(X,V)=(V^X)_0$. The edge inclusion $a:F(1)\to E$ is degreewise injective, so [lem-coef-segal-cartesian-exponent] makes restriction $r:\operatorname{Map}(E,V)\to V_1$ a Kan fibration. In a map $E\to V$, let $f,g$ be the images of $0\to1$ and $1\to0$. The triangles $010$ and $101$ give $[g][f]=1$ and $[f][g]=1$ in $hV$, so $r$ lands in $V_{\mathrm{eq}}$. The endpoint composites are restrictions along $a\circ d^1=e_0$ and $a\circ d^0=e_1$.

source.place: Sections 2.3-2.5 and 6, restriction fibration and the two inverse triangles.

proof.text: For a discrete simplicial space $X$ use $T_V(X)$, the mapping subspace requiring every edge evaluation to lie in $V_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and $H(k)=\bigcup_{i=1}^k d^iF(k-1)$ from [lem-coef-segal-equivalence-outer-horn]. Its restriction $\rho_k:T_V(F(k))\to T_V(H(k))$ is a weak equivalence for $k\geq2$. It is also a Kan fibration: [lem-coef-segal-cartesian-exponent] gives this for the unrestricted mapping spaces, and its inverse image of $T_V(H(k))$ is exactly $T_V(F(k))$. For $k\geq3$, the horn contains every edge of $F(k)$. For $k=2$, its edges $01$ and $02$ are equivalences and its triangle gives $[12][01]=[02]$, hence $[12]=[02][01]^{-1}$ is an equivalence too. Thus the restricted map is a pullback of the unrestricted fibration; projecting any horn lifting square proves it is a fibration. By the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], each $\rho_k$ is consequently a trivial fibration, so has boundary lifting in every inner dimension, including zero.

source.place: Section 11, Lemma 11.10 and its notation; Reedy restriction fibrations from Sections 2.4-2.5.

proof.text:
Let $E(k)$ be the subobject of $E$ generated by the alternating word $0101\cdots$ of length $k+1$, starting at $0$. Then $E(1)=F(1)$ and $E=\bigcup_{k\geq1}E(k)$. For $k\geq2$ its characteristic simplex $\sigma_k:F(k)\to E(k)$ gives
$$E(k)=E(k-1)\amalg_{H(k)}F(k).$$
Indeed the new nondegenerate simplices are precisely the alternating $k$-simplex starting at $0$ and its face $d_0$, the alternating $(k-1)$-simplex starting at $1$. The face $d_k$ already belongs to $E(k-1)$; every face $d_i$, $0<i<k$, has two adjacent equal entries and is a degeneracy of a shorter alternating word. All remaining simplices are degeneracies of these words, which proves the pushout degree by degree.

source.place: Section 11, the filtration preceding Proposition 11.1 and pushout (11.8).

proof.text: Put $T_k=T_V(E(k))$. Then $T_1=V_{\mathrm{eq}}$. For $k=2$, a map $E(2)\to V$ has edges $f:0\to1$, $g:1\to0$ with $[g][f]=1_0$; if $f$ is invertible then $[g]=[f]^{-1}$, so all its edges are equivalences. For $k\geq3$, both words $010$ and $101$ lie in $E(k)$, so both inverse equations hold and every map $E(k)\to V$ belongs to $T_k$. These assertions hold on all inner simplices, since membership in a union of components is determined by its vertices. Therefore $T_k=\operatorname{Map}(E(k),V)$ for $k\geq3$, and $T_V(E)=\operatorname{Map}(E,V)$.

source.place: Section 11.7, the final proof of Proposition 11.1, equivalence-edge subspaces for E(k).

proof.text:
Apply mapping spaces to the pushout in step 3. Since a map on a pushout is a pair agreeing on the overlap, and the edges of $E(k)$ are the union of the images of the edges of $E(k-1)$ and $F(k)$, the same assertion with the all-edges condition gives the strict pullback
$$T_k=T_{k-1}\times_{T_V(H(k))}T_V(F(k)).$$
Thus $T_k\to T_{k-1}$ is a pullback of the trivial fibration $\rho_k$ of step 2. It has boundary lifting: project a prescribed boundary problem to $\rho_k$, fill there, and pair that filler with its prescribed $T_{k-1}$ coordinate. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], these are trivial fibrations for every $k\geq2$.

The equality $E=\bigcup_kE(k)$ gives $\operatorname{Map}(E,V)=\varprojlim_kT_k$: compatible maps glue uniquely in every outer and inner degree, and step 4 identifies the cofinal tail with the unrestricted mapping spaces. The projection to $T_1=V_{\mathrm{eq}}$ has boundary lifting. Given $\partial\Delta^q\to\varprojlim_kT_k$ and its prescribed extension $\Delta^q\to T_1$, recursively lift that simplex to $T_2,T_3,\ldots$ using step 5, retaining at each stage the prescribed boundary. The compatible lifts define a simplex of the inverse limit. This includes $q=0$, when the boundary is empty. The criterion in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes this projection a trivial fibration, hence a weak homotopy equivalence. The projection is restriction along $a$, which is the required $\epsilon_V$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.2 from Proposition 11.1, inverse limit of the tower of trivial fibrations.

proof.text: All restrictions commute with postcomposition by a map of Segal spaces, and such postcomposition preserves inverse triangles; this proves naturality on $V_{\mathrm{eq}}$ as well as on the mapping spaces. The endpoint equalities in step 1 are precomposition identities in every inner degree, so the map is over $V_0^2$. Finally let $p:E\to F(0)$ be collapse. The composite $p\circ a:F(1)\to F(0)$ is the unique map corresponding to $[1]\to[0]$. For every inner simplex $x:c\Delta^q\to V$, precomposition along $p\circ a$ is exactly $s_0x$. Hence the collapse composite equals $s_0$ as a simplicial map, in all degrees.

source.place: Section 6, endpoints and collapse; naturality of precomposition.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 6.2, deduced by the alternating-word filtration (11.8) from Lemma 11.10 and the boundary-lifting inverse-limit argument in Section 11. Archived source WANTED.

The item statement matches Theorem 6.2: same E=discnerve I[1], restriction along x->y, Reedy-fibrant Segal space, no completeness. V_eq equals W_hoequiv by 5.5 and 5.8. The endpoint and collapse clauses are elementary. The statement is unchanged and not weakened. Step 1: the triangles 010 and 101 give both inverse equations, and the endpoint order is right. Step 2: I checked that H(k) contains every edge for k>=3, and that for k=2 the missing edge is [12]=[02][01]^{-1}. So T_V(F(k)) is a pullback of the Kan fibration given by the exponent node, and with the new node it is a trivial fibration by the Kan node. Step 3: Rezk states the pushout without proof, so I checked it degreewise myself. sigma_k is injective outside H(k), because a map onto {1..k} is recovered from its word and starting letter, and its words avoid E(k-1) by reduced length. Steps 4-7 are correctly elementary and match Rezk's proof of 11.1 and the tower argument. New node lem-coef-segal-equivalence-outer-horn: it is exactly Rezk Lemma 11.10 (H(k) is the largest subobject not containing d0 iota, T_V is Map_hoequiv), with the same hypotheses. Tested on k=2 (Lemma 11.6 plus pi_0), empty V, terminal V and nerves of categories. B1-B7 are met, it is strictly smaller than the item, and it is non-elementary. My DAG search found no duplicate: segal-inverse-evaluation is the infinity-categorical analogue, cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling is about quasicategories, cotensor-evaluation-dk is Rezk 13.9.
